data.why: The repo ships no example data (sample_data/ is gitignored and absent at this commit), so a small synthetic MERSCOPE-format dataset (30 cells, 2 types, a crypt/villus/lamina-propria layout) was hand-written as CSV; a generator script installed alongside it produces the binary edges.parquet (NICHESv2 output format) and cell_boundaries.parquet that cannot be authored as plain text.

goals: Load a spatial transcriptomics dataset and confirm which platform was auto-detected and what layers it supports
Toggle individual ligand-receptor mechanisms (LRMs) on and off and see which cell-cell edges carry that signal
Color edges by communication score vs. by cell-type metadata to compare where signal concentrates against tissue structure
Click a cell or an edge to inspect its full expression / LRM detail, including autocrine (self-signalling) rings
Filter cells or edges to a metadata subset (a cell type, a cluster) and confirm a rare subset still renders at full density
Add supplemental per-cell annotations (a cluster label, a pseudotime value) without touching the original platform files and confirm they appear as new color-by options

review.summary: The tree states TissuePlex's purpose correctly (exploring the NICHESv2 ligand–receptor graph on tissue against cell annotations) and its core edge, cell and filter tasks are backed by accurate screens and successful replays. Some specific labels drawn from the Split view are wrong, Split itself is unconfirmed, the edge-metadata filter crash is buried, and several README capabilities are missing (edge-source switching, strength threshold/fade, region cell export, image channels), so it needs fixes before filing.
